scope: Independent offline review of client-candidate diagnostic-emission patch v3
checks: Exact two base/current preimages, frozen postimages and unchanged ownership helper match; full patch and v2-to-v3 delta apply and reverse byte-exactly; whitespace check passes.
All 30 frozen offline Python tests pass independently. Tests include actual owned subprocess simulations, not Rust or Cargo.
Both archived e766 partitionline failure logs replay with their real final summary and panic context after trailing blank lines.

Independent fake-log replay rejects injected status and section lines from the console projection, preserves the complete raw log/receipt and its unchanged raw failure list, bounds long summaries and reports truncation, and suppresses a forged final summary on timeout.
Console diagnostic lines are ASCII and escape command delimiters and control characters; per-block output caps are enforced. JSON summaries remain parseable and escape command delimiters.

Expected baseline failures suppress panic emission; mismatching baselines and failed full-target gates emit scoped diagnostic context. Split compiler stderr and structured compiler messages are handled. Reviewed source changes do not alter test selection, timeouts, raw receipt extraction or gate decisions.
decision: No blocker found in the scoped source and offline review.
limits: No Cargo, Rust compilation, live GitHub API, publication or native qualification.
The output bounds apply per emitted summary/diagnostic block, not to existing in-memory log reads or all output over an entire workflow.
Libtest output is unframed and can be forged, including spoofing a genuine other failure heading; attribution is best effort and no secret redaction is claimed.
The original raw result parser/gating consumes unframed log data as before; console projection is labeled unverified and is not an independent correctness proof.
Missing panic sections, abrupt termination, and a clipped test name can prevent useful context from appearing.
